nodes.title: Note: Usage
widgets_values:
## No-reference scoring (no clean reference needed)

Two images go in through `Batch Images` and the SAME batch runs through three
no-reference metrics - the quickest way to compare models on identical input:

- **pyiqa NR Score** with A-FINE (NR head): **lower is better**, range ~-2 to 2.
- **FGResQ NR Score** with the FGResQ NR variant: **higher is better**, 0-1.
- **QReAlign NR Score** with Q-ReAlign Mini 0.8B (int8_convrot), task
  `aesthetic IAA`: **higher is better**, 0-1. This one judges aesthetics, not
  technical fidelity.

Each score node answers **per image**, so two images in produce two values - the
`Preview as Text` widgets show a list.

## Batch Images: several images, or just one

`Batch Images` is here to show that both ways work. It gathers its inputs into a
single batch and passes that on: connect as many images as you like (it grows a
fresh input as you fill the last one, up to 50), or leave just one connected - one
image is a valid batch of one, and the scores simply come back as a single value.

You do not have to keep it. Wire one image straight into the `image` input of each
score node instead - a `Load Image`, or any other image output such as a `KSampler`
result - and delete `Batch Images`. Nothing else changes.

## How to run

1. Point the `Load Image` nodes at your own images (any size; the pack handles each
   architecture's constraints, e.g. A-FINE needs sides divisible by 32).
2. Queue the prompt - no reference image is involved.
3. Read the three `Preview as Text` widgets.

The first run downloads weights into `ComfyUI/models/pyiqa/` (or a pyiqa folder
from `extra_model_paths.yaml`): A-FINE ~580 MB, FGResQ ~1.2 GB (two files),
Q-ReAlign Mini int8 ~1.6 GB. Q-ReAlign also needs `transformers>=5`; if yours is
older the loader stops and prints the exact `pip install` command.

## Unload Pyiqa Models

This node exists so you can empty the loaded metrics **on demand**, instead of
waiting for the workflow to end or for the next score to swap models around. It
unloads every pyiqa metric the pack has cached, from VRAM and RAM, leaving only
the files on disk - they reload on the next score (seconds for the small metrics,
around 30s for Q-ReAlign Pro). `empty_cuda_cache` is switched on here, so it also
hands PyTorch's reserved-but-unused GPU memory back to the driver.

It is a passthrough: whatever you wire into it comes back out unchanged, so it can
sit anywhere on any wire and never interrupts the graph. In this template it
carries the Q-ReAlign score on to its preview. It touches only this pack's
metrics; ComfyUI's own models stay under ComfyUI's control.

Each score node's `memory_management` widget decides when *its* metric is freed:
`unload model (VRAM + RAM)` (what this template uses) drops it right after
scoring, while `keep loaded` holds it for the next image - faster when scoring
many images with the same metric, since reloading from disk is the slow part.
